landing.pageTitle: code-req · Ask a developer to build your app
landing.metaDescription: Ask a developer to build your app. Free, open source, and self-hostable.
landing.heroTitle: Ask a developer to build your app
landing.heroBody: Describe the app you want, pick a developer, and follow your request until it ships. No account is needed to send a request.
landing.findHelp: Paste a username, or the link a developer shared with you.
landing.notFound: No developer named @{username}. Check the spelling or browse the directory below.
landing.step1Body: Use a developer's link, or search the directory below.
landing.step2Body: Write what you want, pick the platforms, and attach an icon if you have one.
landing.step3Body: Keep your tracking link. You can read the quote, message the developer, and change details until work starts.
landing.myRequestsBody: Requests you sent from this browser. Clearing browser data removes this list, but the tracking links still work.
landing.directoryEmptyBody: Developers appear here after they set up a profile and accept requests.
landing.forDevelopersBody: Create a profile with a username, share your link, and receive requests in one dashboard.
landing.faq1A: Yes. The site and its source code are free. Developers set their own prices.
landing.faq2A: The developer you chose sees it. Contact details you add are visible only to that developer.
landing.faq3Q: Can I change or cancel my request?
landing.faq3A: You can edit it while it is new or in progress, and you can cancel it while it is new.
landing.faq4Q: Why should I keep the tracking link?
landing.faq4A: The tracking link is the only way back to your request unless you use the same browser. Anyone with the link can see that request, so keep it private.

privacy.metaDescription: How code-req stores and shares your data.
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: code-req stores only what it needs to deliver requests between people and developers. It has no advertising, no analytics, and no third-party trackers.
privacy.whatBody: A request keeps the title, description, platforms, optional icon, notes, budget, deadline, and the requester's name. Contact details (email, phone, availability) are stored separately and are readable only by the developer. A developer profile keeps the username, display name, bio, and accepted platforms.
privacy.whoBody: Developers see the requests sent to them. Anyone with a tracking link can see that one request. Developer profiles and portfolios are public. The site's operator can see only what the database rules allow.
privacy.accountsBody: Requesters do not need an account. Submitting a request creates an anonymous session in your browser, so you can find your requests again on this device. Developers sign in with Google or with an email address and password. Anonymous sessions cannot manage requests.
privacy.rightsBody: Developers can export all their data as JSON and delete their account from the dashboard. Requesters can cancel a request while it is new, and they can ask a developer to remove a request.
privacy.cookiesBody: The site stores a few preferences in your browser: language, theme, and the drafts you are writing. It does not set tracking cookies.
